styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: My Khe sand, sunrise swims and seafood by the water.

styles.label: Eats
styles.blurb: Mì Quảng, seafood and night markets, all within easy reach.

styles.label: Heritage
styles.blurb: Cham sculpture, the Marble Mountains and quiet old streets.

stays.why: Closest to the sand and the seafront walk. Many resorts and mid-range hotels. Good base for beach days.
The city centre, near the Dragon Bridge, Han Market and most restaurants. Easy bus and taxi links.
Quiet, green and near the sea. Few shops nearby, so plan on taxis or Grab for dinner. Best for resorts.
Budget guesthouses and cafés. Popular with backpackers and the place to rent a scooter or bike.

food: Try mì Quảng, the local turmeric noodle dish with a little broth, and bánh xèo, the crispy pancake.
Han Market is the easiest place to sample fresh seafood and local snacks in one visit.
Eat at busy local stalls. Pick the places with a queue of locals and plastic stools.
Seafood restaurants along the beach road are good for dinner. Check prices on the menu before ordering.
Ask for water and ice carefully. Stick to bottled water if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Ba Na Hills: a mountain resort with a long cable car ride. Check prices and opening times on the day.
Hoi An: an old trading town about 45 minutes away by car or taxi, depending on traffic. Good for a half-day or evening.
Marble Mountains: stone caves and small temples close to the beach. Easy to add to a half-day, with a taxi or bike.

recommend.why: Two nights give you a beach day, a food walk and a Marble Mountains or Hoi An trip without rushing.

month_notes: January: Cool at 20–24°C with about 20 rain days. Pack a light jacket and plan indoor sights on wet days.
February: Mild at 20–24°C with about 13 rain days. Good for sightseeing and motorbike trips.
March: Warm at 22–27°C with about 10 rain days. One of the best months for beaches and outings.
April: Hot at 24–30°C with about 8 rain days. The driest month, so good for beaches and motorbike rides.
May: Hot at 26–32°C with about 13 rain days. Start early for outdoor plans and bring sunscreen.
June: Very hot at 27–34°C with about 10 rain days. Swim in the morning and rest in the heat of the afternoon.
July: Hot at 27–33°C with about 16 rain days. Expect some short showers, so keep a light rain jacket handy.
August: Hot at 27–33°C with about 17 rain days. Warm sea and frequent short storms, so plan flexible days.
September: Warm at 26–31°C with about 22 rain days. Rain picks up, so pack a rain jacket and focus on food and museums.
October: Mild at 24–28°C with about 26 rain days. Wet month, so plan indoor visits and check the forecast daily.
November: Cool at 23–27°C with about 24 rain days. Wet and breezy; good for museums and cafés.
December: Cool at 21–24°C with about 25 rain days. Lots of rain, so pack waterproof gear and plan indoor days.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical coastal climate: hot, humid and sunny from spring to summer, with a wetter season from autumn to early winter.

items.title: Best time: March to August
items.text: Mostly dry days at 24–34°C with fewer rain days. Good for beaches, sea swims and motorbike trips.

items.title: Wet season: September to December
items.text: Rain falls on 22–26 days a month. Showers come and go, so plan indoor sights and keep rain gear in your bag.

items.title: Hot afternoons (May to August)
items.text: Highs reach 32–34°C. Do outdoor sights before 11:00 and rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Humidity year-round
items.text: Air feels heavy, especially near the sea. Carry water and wear light, breathable clothes.

items.title: Sea conditions change
items.text: Waves can be rough in the wet months. Check local warnings and follow lifeguard flags at the beach.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a hat, strong sunscreen, a compact rain jacket and a light layer for air-conditioned rooms. Bring modest clothes for temples.

transit.best: Grab or taxi for most trips; city buses if you are saving money and have time.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Do not plan around rail in the city.
19 new, air-conditioned local bus lines with a flat 8,000 ₫ fare inside city limits. Use the DanaBus app or danangbus.vn for routes. Avoid the look-alike danabus.vn site, which has outdated prices.
Mai Linh, Vinasun and Song Han are reliable taxi firms. Grab is widely used and shows prices upfront.
Cheap for short hops. Helmets are required by law, so insist the driver gives you one.
Driving is chaotic, so many visitors hire a car with a driver instead of driving themselves.
Rent a scooter or 4-speed bike near Tran Cao Van. Electric bicycles need no licence and suit city travel.
Works well along the beach and in central streets.
